'''David Bennett Madigan''' (born 11 December 1962) is an Irish-American statistician and academic. He is currently Professor of Statistics and [[Senior advisor|Special Advisor]] to the President at [[Northeastern University]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Diaz |first=Lauren |url=https://www.khoury.northeastern.edu/people/david-madigan/ |title=David Madigan, Professor |publisher=khoury.northeastern.edu |date=2025-07-07 |accessdate=2025-07-08}}</ref> From 2020 to 2025 he was Provost and Senior Vice-President for Academic Affairs at [[Northeastern University]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.northeastern.edu/2020/03/23/david-madigan-appointed-as-northeastern-university-provost-and-senior-vice-president-for-academic-affairs/|title=News@Northeastern|date=24 March 2020 }}</ref> Previously he was Professor of [[Statistics]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://stat.columbia.edu/department-directory/name/david-madigan/|title=David Madigan » Department Directory}}</ref> at [[Columbia University]]. From 2013 to 2018 he was also the Executive Vice-President for Arts and Sciences and Dean of the Faculty of Arts and Sciences<ref>{{cite web |url=http://fas.columbia.edu/home/about-faculty-arts-and-sciences/welcome-message-executive-vice-president |title=Welcome message from the Executive Vice President &#124; Faculty of Arts and Sciences |publisher=Fas.columbia.edu |date= |accessdate=2015-11-20 |archive-date=6 September 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150906054651/http://fas.columbia.edu/home/about-faculty-arts-and-sciences/welcome-message-executive-vice-president |url-status=dead }}</ref> and from 2008 to 2013 he served as Chair of the  Department of [[Statistics]], both at [[Columbia University]]. He was Dean of [[Physical and Mathematical Sciences]] at [[Rutgers University]] (2005–2007), Director of the Institute of Biostatistics at [[Rutgers University]] (2003–2004), and Professor in the Department of [[Statistics]] at [[Rutgers University]] (2001–2007).

==Education==
Madigan received his [[bachelor's degree]] in [[mathematics]] (1984, First Class Honours, Gold Medal) and a [[Ph.D.]] in [[statistics]] (1990), both from [[Trinity College Dublin]].  His Ph.D. thesis, titled ''An Investigation of Weights of Evidence in the Context of Probablilistic Expert Systems'', was written under the supervision of Krzysztof Mosurski.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=22275}}</ref>

==Career==
===Early career===
Madigan began his academic career in the 1990s at the [[University of Washington]] where he was an Assistant and then Associate Professor of [[Statistics]]. He received the University's Distinguished Teaching Award in 1995.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.washington.edu/teaching/awards/awards-recipients |title=Distinguished Teaching Award Previous award recipients |publisher=www.washington.edu |date= |accessdate=2016-02-18}}</ref> Madigan has also served as Vice President, Data Mining, Soliloquy, Inc. (2000-2001), Principal Technical Staff Member, [[AT&T Labs]]-Research (1999-2000), [[Information technology consulting|Information Technology Consultant]], [[KPMG]] (1989-1990), Technology Manager, Peregrine Expert Systems Ltd. (1986-1989), Expert System Consultant, [[SkillSoft]], (1985-1986), and Actuarial Associate, Hibernian Life Assurance, [[Ireland]] (1984-1985).{{citation needed|date=January 2020}}

Advancement of Science]] (2012), a Fellow of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] (2006),<ref>{{cite web |url=http://imstat.org/awards/honored_fellows.htm |title=Institute of Mathematical Statistics Honored Fellows |publisher=www.imstat.org |date= |accessdate=2016-02-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161019175343/http://imstat.org/awards/honored_fellows.htm |archive-date=2016-10-19 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and a Fellow of the [[American Statistical Association]] (1999).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.amstat.org/awards/fellowslist.cfm |title=American Statistical Association Fellows |publisher=www.amstat.org |date= |accessdate=2016-02-18 |archive-date=16 June 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160616161612/https://www.amstat.org/awards/fellowslist.cfm |url-status=dead }}</ref> He has served as program co-chair for the FODS,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://fods.acm.org |title=ACM-IMS Foundations of Data Science Conference|publisher=www.acm.org |date= |accessdate=2020-02-29}}</ref> KDD<ref>{{cite |accessdate=2019-12-05}}</ref> and AI-STATS conferences,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gatsby.ucl.ac.uk/aistats/workshops.html |title=Workshops on AI and Statistics|publisher=www.gatsby.ucl.ac.uk |date= |accessdate=2019-12-05}}</ref> Action Editor for the [[Journal of Machine Learning Research]], Editor-in-Chief of [[Statistical Science]], and Editor-in-Chief of [[Statistical Analysis and Data === Scholarship ===
He has over 200 publications<ref>{{cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?sortby=pubdate&hl=en&user=XDajlywAAAAJ&view_op=list_works|title=David Madigan's Publications from Google Scholar|date= |accessdate=2018-06-26}}</ref> in such areas as [[Bayesian statistics]], [[text mining]], [[Monte Carlo methods]], [[pharmacovigilance]] and probabilistic [[graphical models]]. He has advised 18 Ph.D. students.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=22275|title=David Bennett Madigan|publisher=www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu|date= |accessdate=2020-07-04}}</ref> In recent years he has focused on statistical methodology for generating reliable evidence from large-scale healthcare data.<ref>{{cite journal|title=A Systematic Statistical Approach to Evaluating Evidence from Observational Studies|publisher=www.annualreviews.org|doi=10.1146/annurev-statistics-022513-115645|bibcode=2014AnRSA...1...11M|year=2014|last1=Madigan|first1=David|last2=Stang|first2=Paul E.|last3=Berlin|first3=Jesse A.|last4=Schuemie|first4=Martijn|last5=Overhage|first5=J. Marc|last6=Suchard|first6=Marc A.|last7=Dumouchel|first7=Bill|last8=Hartzema|first8=Abraham G.|last9=Ryan|first9=Patrick B.|journal=Annual Review of Statistics and Its Application|volume=1|issue=1|pages=11–39|doi-access=free}}</ref> From 2011 to 2014 he was a member of the FDA's Drug Safety and Risk Management Advisory Committee.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fda.gov/downloads/AdvisoryCommittees/CommitteesMeetingMaterials/Drugs/DrugSafetyandRiskManagementAdvisoryCommittee/UCM270956.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110908232332/http://www.fda.gov/downloads/AdvisoryCommittees/CommitteesMeetingMaterials/Drugs/DrugSafetyandRiskManagementAdvisoryCommittee/UCM270956.pdf|url-status=dead|archive-date=8 September 2011|title=DSaRM Roster|publisher=www.fda.gov|date= |accessdate=2016-10-26}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Madigan grew up in [[Athlone]] in the center of [[Ireland]], where he attended the [[Marist Brothers]] schools.{{Citation needed|date=February 2022}}
